title: Meta says its AI is making you spend more time on Instagram
excerpt: Meta says people are spending more time on Instagram, and it credits its artificial intelligence for the increase. Global time spent on the app grew by double digits year on year in the second quarter, the company told investors, driven by AI-tuned recommendations in the main feed and in Reels. The gains are specific enough […]
content_html:
Meta says people are spending more time on Instagram, and it credits its artificial intelligence for the increase. Global time spent on the app grew by double digits year on year in the second quarter, the company told investors, driven by AI-tuned recommendations in the main feed and in Reels.

The gains are specific enough to be measured. Meta said a reworked Reels system lifted sessions by 15 basis points, a small-sounding figure that, across billions of users, translates into a meaningful amount of extra attention captured.

The pattern holds across Meta’s apps. Video time has surged on both Instagram and Facebook, the company said, as short-form recommendations pull users from the feeds they follow toward an endless stream the algorithm assembles for them.

Mark Zuckerberg described the change as more personal, not just more. “Our recommendations are also becoming more personalized, surfacing more fresh content while giving people more direct control over what they see,” he said, pairing the engagement gains with a nod to user choice.

The technical shift underneath is notable. Zuckerberg said Reels now combines faster inference with a new architecture that draws on a deeper history of what each user has done, letting the system predict more accurately what will keep them watching.

Meta has also turned large language models loose on its own feed. The company now runs every public Reel and post through an LLM to analyse its topic and tone, which Zuckerberg called “a key building block toward greater personalization,” with plans to extend it to Facebook.

The purpose is plain enough. Understanding content more deeply lets Meta match it more precisely to each viewer, and more precise matching means more time spent, the metric on which its advertising business ultimately rests.

That is where the achievement becomes uncomfortable. The same design Meta celebrates as personalisation is the one that regulators and litigants describe as engineered compulsion, especially where younger users are concerned.

The lawsuits are not abstract. Meta booked a $2.4 billion legal charge in the quarter, and a group of US states is pressing claims that its products are built to keep young people hooked, litigation that turns “time spent” from a boast into evidence.

Meta’s answer is that control comes with the engagement. Executives point to settings that let users tune their own algorithms and to teen-specific protections rolled out across its apps, arguing that more personalisation need not mean less agency.

Critics see the two claims as hard to hold together. A system optimised to maximise time spent, they argue, is not neutral about what a user “chooses,” and the controls sit on top of an engine designed to keep people scrolling.

For the business, though, the direction is unambiguous. Engagement is the raw material of Meta’s ad machine, and anything that reliably lifts it, especially AI that does so at scale, is exactly what the company has been spending tens of billions to build.

More time also means more inventory. Every extra minute of scrolling is another slot Meta can sell to advertisers, which is why engagement gains translate so directly into the revenue that funds everything else.

It also helps explain the spending. Meta’s enormous AI capex is often framed around future agents and superintelligence, but the clearest near-term payoff is this, a recommendation system that already measurably increases how long people stay.

The tension will follow Meta into court and onto the balance sheet. The AI that lifts engagement is both its best answer to investors asking where the returns are and its worst evidence in cases asking whether those returns come at users’ expense.

For now, the number is going up. People are spending more time on Instagram, Meta knows exactly why, and the same fact that reassures Wall Street is the one its opponents intend to use against it.

content_html_zh:
Meta 表示，人们在 Instagram 上花费的时间越来越多，这一增长归功于其人工智能。 该公司告诉投资者，在主要提要和 Reels 中经过人工智能调整的推荐的推动下，第二季度全球用户在该应用上花费的时间同比增长了两位数。

收益足够具体，可以衡量。 Meta 表示，经过重新设计的 Reels 系统将会话数提高了 15 个基点，这个数字听起来很小，但对于数十亿用户来说，却意味着获得了大量的额外关注。

这种模式适用于 Meta 的应用程序。 该公司表示，Instagram 和 Facebook 上的视频时间都在激增，因为简短的推荐将用户从他们关注的信息流中拉向算法为他们收集的源源不断的信息流。

马克·扎克伯格将这一变化描述为更加个性化，而不仅仅是更多。 “我们的推荐也变得更加个性化，呈现更多新鲜内容，同时让人们更直接地控制他们所看到的内容，”他说，将参与度提升与对用户选择的认可结合起来。

下面的技术转变是值得注意的。 扎克伯格表示，Reels 现在将更快的推理与新架构结合起来，该架构利用每个用户所做操作的更深入历史记录，让系统更准确地预测他们会观看的内容。

Meta 还让大型语言模型在自己的源上变得松散。 该公司现在通过法学硕士来运行每个公共 Reel 和帖子，以分析其主题和语气，扎克伯格称其为“实现更大个性化的关键组成部分”，并计划将其扩展到 Facebook。

目的很明显。 更深入地了解内容可以让 Meta 更精确地将其与每个观看者匹配，而更精确的匹配意味着花费更多的时间，这是其广告业务最终依赖的指标。

这就是成就变得令人不舒服的地方。 Meta 所推崇的个性化设计也被监管机构和诉讼当事人描述为工程强制，尤其是对于年轻用户而言。

这些诉讼并不抽象。 Meta 在本季度收到了 24 亿美元的法律指控，美国一些州正在敦促其产品是为了让年轻人着迷而设计的，诉讼将“花费的时间”从吹嘘变成了证据。

Meta 的答案是，控制力伴随着参与度而来。 高管们指出，允许用户调整自己的算法的设置，以及在其应用程序中推出的针对青少年的保护措施，认为更多的个性化并不意味着更少的代理。

批评者认为这两种说法很难结合在一起。 他们认为，一个经过优化以最大化花费时间的系统对于用户“选择”的内容并不是中立的，并且控件位于旨在让人​​们滚动的引擎顶部。

但对于企业来说，方向是明确的。 参与度是 Meta 广告机器的原材料，任何能够可靠地提升它的东西，尤其是大规模的人工智能，正是该公司花费数百亿美元打造的东西。

更多的时间也意味着更多的库存。 每多滚动一分钟，Meta 就可以向广告商出售另一个插槽，这就是为什么参与度收益可以直接转化为为其他一切提供资金的收入。

它还有助于解释支出。 Meta 巨大的人工智能资本支出通常围绕未来的代理和超级智能展开，但最明显的近期回报是这个，一个已经显着增加人们停留时间的推荐系统。

这种紧张局势将随着梅塔进入法庭并影响到资产负债表。 提高参与度的人工智能既是投资者询问回报在哪里的最佳答案，也是在询问这些回报是否以用户为代价的情况下最糟糕的证据。

目前，这个数字正在上升。 人们在 Instagram 上花费的时间越来越多，Meta 清楚地知道其中的原因，而让华尔街放心的事实正是其反对者打算用来对付它的事实。
